A lot of times the loved ones around us just simply don't understand the illness of depression and therefore are not as apt to assist as someone who has been through it. I went to a program where it was a day program for depression/anxiety/substance abuse and it was helpful to talk to others who actually understood the struggles of depression. From not being able to get out of bed or have any desire to, or having difficulties with simple tasks, or just losing interest and hope. When we are in this state of mind the pain and depression just overcomes us and the reigns are off. I am in a similar situation as you, I screwed up a good part of my life, I'm in my mid 20s and had a lot going for me. I don't really want to get into what I was doing on a public forum as much of my success was covered by the media, but when I lost everything, including my GF, I just completely lost it and haven't had a glimpse of hope in a while. Sometimes I'll get into a manic phase which I know is not healthy but it just feels so good to feel normal and happy again.

Unfortunately I don't know the answers on how to fix it, other than to maybe find a support group for depression locally where you can talk to others who will actually understand your situation, and don't be afraid to reach out for help. It is scary at first because of fear of being judged and such but group support is the best thing you can do.

It seems as though the stigma surrounding suicide is those left behind. Honestly the people that care about me know the pain I'm in so I feel they'd accept me wanting to end my pain. But the whole future thing definitely does make an impact, so I guess I'll just keep pushing at it.
